# Thermostat view

> Overview type `climate` (since 1.1). Entity: required, a `climate` entity. Card type `custom:houseview-climate-overview-card` (widget type `climate_overview`), screensaver `type: climate`.

A full-screen thermostat for a Home Assistant `climate.*` entity: the name and the time along the top, "Cooling to" or
"Heating to" over the target in very large figures with a down and an up key beside it, the room temperature and
humidity beneath, and top right a three-dot key that opens Home Assistant's own dialog for the entity (power,
modes, fan, presets). The whole view takes one flat colour: blue while cooling, orange while heating, slate while the
unit rests, grey when it is off.

It opens when you press the number on a [thermostat widget](../widgets/climate.md) and closes with the key top left or
Escape. Unlike a screensaver it is a **control panel**: its keys stay live, a press on the background does nothing, and
the view follows the thermostat while it is up. Turn the view off with `climate_view: false` on the carousel; the
number then opens the entity dialog, as it did before. It also works as a page card or a standalone card
(`custom:houseview-climate-overview-card`) with the same keys and no close key.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entity | entity | required | A `climate.*` entity |
| name | text | friendly name | The title |
| show_time | boolean | true | The time, below the name |

```yaml
type: custom:houseview-card
cards:
  - type: custom:houseview-climate-card
    entity: climate.living_room
    name: Living Room
```

A `screensaver` entry of `type: climate` written in YAML supplies the options (`show_time: false`); the view is not
offered in the editor's screensaver list, since an idle screensaver that only wakes on a press is not what a control
panel is for.

## What is shown

| Thermostat | Caption | Number | Keys |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hvac_action: cooling` (or mode `cool` without an action) | Cooling to | the target | step |
| `hvac_action: heating` (or mode `heat`) | Heating to | the target | step |
| `hvac_action: idle` / `fan`, other modes | Set to | the target | step |
| `heat_cool` | Heat to 19° · Cool to 24° | the room temperature | disabled |
| no numeric target | Set to | the room temperature | disabled |
| `off` | Off | the target, dimmed | step |
| unavailable or unknown | Unavailable | — | disabled |

* **Down / up.** Each press runs the thermostat widget's own `down` / `up` action, so the step (`target_temp_step`,
  else 1 °F or 0.5 °C), the clamping to `min_temp` / `max_temp` and the rounding are the same as on the widget. The keys
  are disabled without a numeric target, without target-temperature support (`supported_features` bit 1) and at the
  limits.
* **Figures.** The room temperature (`current_temperature`) with a degree sign and the humidity (`current_humidity`) as a
  percentage; a figure the entity does not report is left out. Numbers are formatted for your language with at most
  one decimal.
* **Three-dot details key.** Opens the more-info dialog of the entity, over the view. Disabled only when the entity does not
  exist.
* **Time.** The clock below the name follows your Home Assistant time format and zone and is patched once a minute.

## Cost

Painted with CSS only (one flat colour, text, two chevrons drawn with borders and four icons): no images, gradients,
filters or animation, so it makes no difference between `performance` modes and has no motion to reduce. The only
JavaScript is the once-a-minute clock on the shared ticker; the keys go through the card's ordinary dispatcher.
